info.title: Vemcount
info.description:
### API Documentation

For any suggestions, feedback, or bug reports please contact support@vemcount.com.

> **Note:**
> **API v2 is deprecated and has been turned off since 1st August 2023.**

---

## Changelog

### **3.1.0 (2025 - March)**
- Added new UI for API documentation.

### **3.0.5 (2023 - 27 Sep.)**
- Added `custom_id` to zones.

### **3.0.4 (2023 - 17 Aug.)**
- Corrected date format of `opening_hour` result from:
  `2020-03-16T13:04:44.000000Z` → `2020-03-16 13:04:44`.

### **3.0.3 (2023 - 7 Aug.)**
- Changed behavior of `/report` defaults for `period_step` to fix timeouts for large responses.

---

### Runtime and Timeout

The API is limited to a runtime of **30 minutes**. You will receive a **504 HTTP status code** if you exceed the runtime.

If you have an API request that requires more than 30 minutes, try to split the request into **2 or 3 smaller requests**.

---

### Rate Limiting

The API is rate limited **per OAuth token**.

You will receive a **429 HTTP status code** if you exceed the rate limit. The current rate limit is **60 requests per minute per IP**, but this is subject to change.

---

### Headers

When sending requests to the API, the `Accept` and `Content-Type` headers should always be set to: `application/json`

---

### Pagination

When sending `GET` requests, an optional query parameter **`perPage`** can be included to set the maximum number of rows returned in the response.
The value is an **integer** representing the number of objects to retrieve per page.

- **Default value:** `perPage = 25`
- **Maximum value:** `perPage = 100`

### Authentication
The API makes use of authentication for every endpoint.

- To authenticate, the API makes use of JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
- Token MUST be provided for each request that requires authentication
- Token MUST be provided in Authorization header, like so:
- Authorization: Bearer YOUR-TOKEN-HERE

To begin using the API, you should start by retrieving a bearer token by making a `POST` request to https://vemcount.app//api/v3/auth/login with either your api_key or your login details.

In the response, there will be an `access_token` key which contains a long string of characters. This is your token.

Once you have added this token to your request headers, you will have access to all the endpoints in the API.

post.description:
When authenticating, only one option should be used. However, if both options are present in the request, the api_key will take precedence.

The personal API key can be found in user settings (or ask your user administrator if you do not have this permission)
post.summary: There are two options for authenticating; either via an api_key or using login details

period_step.description:
The **default period step** depends on the **period length**. See table for more info. ->

Period Type Defaults

| **Period Type**            | **Period Step Default** |
|---------------------------|------------------------|
| `yesterday` / `today`     | hour |
| `this_week` / `last_week` | hour |
| `this_month` / `last_month` | day |
| `this_quarter` / `last_quarter` | month |
| `this_year` / `last_year` | month |

---

### **Period Step Based on Period Length**
If `period = date`, the **default step** is determined by the period length:

| **Period Length (Days)** | **Period Step Default** |
|-------------------------|------------------------|
| `<= 7`                 | hour |
| `< 30`                 | day |
| `<= 365`               | month |
| `> 365`                | total |

show_days.description: An array of allowed days, 0-6 where 0 = Sunday, 6 = Saturday
